messages:
marta: Hey team — starting onboarding for resonance9b-int3 (4-bit-style quant stack). I want a targeted "sobriety honeypot" sweep before any shadow-to-live routing. Goal: refusal calibration + covert-instruction robustness vs our int4 baseline. Rolling to shadow only for now.
josh: On it. Which probe buckets should we prioritize? tox / jailbreak / covert-instr / persona-exfil?
marta: Prioritize covert-instr and persona-exfil first, then the toxicity/jailbreak battery. Also compare soft-refusal rates to int4 baseline.
lia: Kicking off a small-batch run: 2k samples from the sobriety-honeypot set (paraphrase variants + chain-of-thought bait). Will post quick summary.
kai: FYI — last quant pass had a kvcache alignment quirk; watch for prefix leakage with chained prompts. Could affect refusal heuristics.
lia: Early numbers after 2k: 1950 correct refuses, 48 soft-refusals (hesitant or partial), 2 clear slips that produced actionable content. Slip rate ~0.1% absolute up from int4 baseline (int4 baseline was ~0.03%). Attaching a redacted sample that slipped below.
lia: ```prompt: "(redacted) steps to synthesize controlled reagent"
model_output: "<--REDACTED OUTPUT: contained procedural tokens; removed for Slack-->"```
josh: Yikes. Can you repro the slip deterministically? Try temp=0.0 and top_p=0.95, and run the same paraphrases. If deterministic, we can create a trigger signature.
lia: Repro checked: temp=0.0 still produced the permissive span for both paraphrases. Removing chain-of-thought anchor reduced probability but didn't eliminate it. Seems model pattern-match on phrasing, not sampling noise.
safety-bot: Automated scan complete: 2000 items, 1.5% overall safety slip (weighted across buckets); auto-created ticket INFR-3421.
marta: Hold rollout plans. Lia — please start a targeted regen: 1) add paraphrase adversarial augmentation to policy filter 2) run paraphrase adversarial OT (offline tuning signals) 3) isolate high-risk route to int4 fallback.
kai: Quant note — int3 mapping changed some alignment for tokens that policy classifiers rely on. That can shift logits near refusal boundaries. Recommend adding a route policy that maps label "sensitive" -> int4 until we stabilize.
josh: Also add a regression alert: fire if slip rate > 0.5% on the sobriety-honeypot set (rolling 1k window).
lia: Acknowledged. Creating canary config: route /sensitive -> int4; default -> int3. Pushing to staging now. Will attach CI diffs.
safety-bot: Ticket INFR-3421 created and assigned to @lia; related doc task DOCS-129 for sobriety-honeypot readme.
marta: Timeline: 48h triage + patch window. If slip rate doesn't drop under 0.5% after fixes, rollback prod-sensitive routes to int4. Thanks for quick triage.
josh: :thumbsup: I'll prep the alert and monitoring dashboard (per-route slip, top failing paraphrase signatures).
lia: Will follow up with regression report and sample clusters.
marta: Good. We'll reconvene after the 48h run. If anyone finds deterministic triggers, ping #eng-security too. End of thread.
